classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an unknown radius and an auxiliary radius to a chord endpoint, express the perpendicular distance as r−1, and form a Pythagorean equation whose squared-radius terms cancel.

content.prompt: $OP$ is perpendicular to the chord $AB$. If $AB = 14\text{ cm}$ and $PQ = 1\text{ cm}$, find the radius of the circle.

spec.description: Vertical radius OP crosses horizontal chord AB at Q. The right-angle mark and all point labels are retained. Source schematic proportions are retained without asserting scale.
spec.mathematics: OP is a radius perpendicular to AB; AB = 14 cm and PQ = 1 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The radius is unknown; no supplied answer appears.

answer.worked:
Let the radius be $r\text{ cm}$. The perpendicular from the centre bisects $AB$, so $AQ = 7\text{ cm}$ and $OQ = (r-1)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}(r-1)^2+7^2 &= r^2\\r^2-2r+1+49 &= r^2\\50 &= 2r\\r &= 25\end{align*}$$
The radius is $25\text{ cm}$.
